SubTopics: Explain that differences in the apparent brightness of the sun compared to other stars is due to their relative distances from the Earth.
Content: The distances of several stars from `text(Earth)` are shown in the table.
problems/TN25G5Sa/media/1a.jpg
Which of these describes what will be seen when looking at the stars from `text(Earth)`?

A.Choice: Capella appears brighter than Sirius but dimmer than Polaris when viewed from `text(Earth)`.

B.Choice: Spica appears dimmer than Polaris but brighter than Capella when viewed from `text(Earth)`.

C.Choice: Capella appears brighter than Spica but dimmer than Sirius when viewed from `text(Earth)`.

D.Choice: Polaris appears brighter than Spica but dimmer than Capella when viewed from `text(Earth)`.

SubTopics: Use data to categorize different bodies in our solar system including moons, asteroids, comets, and meteoroids according to their physical properties and motion.
Content: Students use a desk lamp to model light from the `text(Sun)`. The students use a globe to model `text(Earth)`. The students shine the light from the desk lamp onto the globe.
problems/TN25G5Sa/media/5a.jpg
The students want to model the reason that the `text(Sun)` appears to rise and set on `text(Earth)`.
Which of these should the students do with the parts of the model?

A.Choice: Spin the globe on its stand.

B.Choice: Turn the desk lamp on and off.

C.Choice: Lift the desk lamp above the globe.

D.Choice: Carry the globe in a circle around the desk lamp.

SubTopics: Distinguish between inherited characteristics and those characteristics that result from a direct interaction with the environment. Apply this concept by giving examples of characteristics of living organisms that are influenced by both inheritance and the environment.
Content: Students place `text(four)` bean seeds into a pot. All of the seeds sprout roots and shoots. The plants have green leaves and stems with white flowers. The mature plants produce long bean pods.
Which `ultext(three)` plant characteristics are `ultext(most likely)` a result of interactions with the environment?

A.Choice: All of the seeds sprout roots that grow down.

B.Choice: If the plants are not watered, they start to droop.

C.Choice: The mature plants produce long green pods containing beans.

D.Choice: The plants have green stems, green leaves, and white flowers.

E.Choice: The shoots all bend to grow toward the only source of sunlight.

SubTopics: Use evidence to support that the gravitational force exerted by Earth on objects is directed toward the Earth's center.
Content: Which statement `ultext(best)` compares the force of gravity acting on the airplane in Figure `1` (Part `1`) and the spacecraft in Figure `2` (Part `1`)?

M.Choice: the force of gravity on the plane is upwards while the force of gravity on the spacecraft is forwards

P.Choice: the force of gravity is towards the center of the `text(Earth)` for both the airplane and the spacecraft

R.Choice: the force of gravity is forwards for the airplane and upwards for the spacecraft

S.Choice: the force of gravity is towards the surface of the `text(Earth)` for both the airplane and the spacecraft

SubTopics: Use evidence to support that the gravitational force exerted by Earth on objects is directed toward the Earth's center.
Content: Which claim is `ultext(most)` supported by evidence in Figure `1` and Figure `2` (Part `1`)?

A.Choice: `text(Earth's)` gravity only affects objects on the surface of `text(Earth)`.

B.Choice: An object being pulled toward `text(Earth's)` center can move in a curved path.

C.Choice: `text(Earth)` only pulls on objects when they are moving away from the surface of `text(Earth)`.

SubTopics: Use evidence to support that the gravitational force exerted by Earth on objects is directed toward the Earth's center.
Content: Based on Figure `3` (Part `2`), which statement `ultext(best)` describes why the people riding the drop tower can feel weightless?

M.Choice: The people and the drop vehicle are both moving in the direction that gravity pulls.

R.Choice: The people and the drop vehicle are both moving too quickly for gravity to affect them.

S.Choice: The force of gravity decreases because the people and the drop vehicle move in opposite directions.

T.Choice: The force of gravity between `text(Earth)` and both the people and the drop vehicle is too small to affect them.

SubTopics: Test the effects of balanced and unbalanced forces on the speed and direction of motion of objects.
Content: When the drop vehicle approaches the bottom of the drop tower, the drop vehicle begins slowing down. During this time, the force on the people is much greater than the force of gravity. Based on Figure `3` (Part `2`), which statement `ultext(best)` describes a reason for this increase in force?

A.Choice: The drop vehicle is at the closest point in its drop to `text(Earth's)` surface.

B.Choice: The force slowing the drop vehicle is in a direction that is away from `text(Earth's)` center.

C.Choice: The force of gravity on the people increases because the drop vehicle is moving toward `text(Earth's)` surface.

D.Choice: The force of gravity starts to pull on the people when the drop vehicle begins moving away from `text(Earth's)` center.
